messages.content: 请帮我检索一下'红星科技'公司目前所有未解决的工单，我想要查看最多10个。

function.name: get_tickets
function.description: Retrieve a list of tickets for a specified customer based on the company name. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

customer.description: The name of the company for which to retrieve tickets.

status.description: The status of the tickets to be retrieved.

limit.description: The maximum number of tickets to retrieve.

The function get_tickets expects status options: "open" | "closed" | "pending" | "resolved". There's no "unresolved" but we can interpret unresolved as "open" or "pending"? Usually unresolved means not resolved, so could be "open" or "pending". But the function only accepts those four statuses. We need to choose one. The user says "未解决" meaning not resolved. That could be "open" or "pending". We might ask clarifying question? But the instruction says we should not ask clarifying questions unless necessary. The user specifically said "未解决" and wants to see all unresolved tickets. The function only supports "open", "closed", "pending", "resolved". So we can interpret unresolved as "open" or "pending". But we need to decide. Maybe we can combine both? But the function only allows one status. We could choose "open" as default. But maybe "pending" also counts as unresolved. The user didn't specify which status. We could ask clarifying question: "Do you mean tickets with status 'open' or 'pending'?" But the instruction says we should not ask clarifying questions unless necessary. Is it necessary? The user said "未解决" which could be interpreted as "open" or "pending". But we can assume "open" is the default. The function's default status is "open". So we can call get_tickets with customer='红星科技', status='open', limit=10. That will retrieve up to 10 open tickets. That seems reasonable.
